turns.question: Did Apex give a valid force majeure notice?
turns.text:
Apex gave a notice of a Force Majeure Event. The notice was sent by email on June 2, 2026, by Apex's Program Manager, Priya Raman, to Morgan's Project Contact, Owen Tremblay [1].

The notice described the event and the expected delivery of the replacement Units on June 10, 2026 [1].

According to Apex, the notice satisfied clause 8.2 of the Services Agreement and it is entitled to relief under clause 8.3 for the whole period from May 21, 2026 to June 10, 2026 [1].

Clause 8.2 of the Services Agreement requires the Affected Party to give written notice within five Business Days after it first becomes aware of the Force Majeure Event. The notice must state that it is given under clause 8.2 and must describe the event, the obligations affected, its expected duration, and the steps taken to mitigate it [6].

Apex gave notice on June 2, 2026, which was within five Business Days of May 21, 2026, the date the flood occurred [1].

The Delivery Date was amended to May 20, 2026, as stated in Amendment No. 1, ¶ 1.1 [6]. Delivery was completed on June 10, 2026 [6]. The period of delay is 21 days, or exactly 3 weeks [6].

The liquidated damages rate was amended to 1.5% of the Total Contract Price for each week of delay [4]. The Total Contract Price is USD 1,240,000 [6].

The weekly liquidated damages amount is 1.5% of USD 1,240,000, which equals USD 18,600 [6]. For 3 weeks of delay, the total liquidated damages before the cap is 3 × USD 18,600 = USD 55,800 [6].

The cap on liquidated damages is 10% of the Total Contract Price, which is USD 124,000 [6]. Since USD 55,800 is less than the cap, the total liquidated damages are USD 55,800 [6].

turns.question: Which units were rejected, why, and which units replaced them?
turns.text:
The rejected units were IC450-1113 and IC450-1134. Unit IC450-1113 was rejected because of a cracked condenser housing, and Unit IC450-1134 was rejected due to a refrigerant leak at a brazed joint in circuit 2 [3].

The units that replaced the rejected ones were IC450-1141 and IC450-1142. These replacement units were delivered on June 10, 2026, and passed inspection on June 11, 2026 [1].

turns.question: What did Simone Achterberg learn from her phone call with Apex?
turns.text: Simone Achterberg learned from her phone call with Apex that the delivery was still on schedule. She called Marcus Delacroix, Shipping Supervisor at Apex, on May 14, 2026, to check the status of the delivery. Mr. Delacroix told her that both trailers were at the Quillon hub, that the drivers had changed there, and that the trailers would leave the hub that night and arrive "first thing Friday" for the 07:30 slot. He gave her the trailer numbers, QFL-5531 and QFL-5547 [3].

turns.question: What case does the research memo rely on for the enforceability of the liquidated damages clause, and can we rely on it?
turns.text:
The research memo relies on the case *Larkspur Hydraulics Corp. v. Vantrell Fabrication Co.*, 284 A.3d 1176 (Del. 2022) for the enforceability of the liquidated damages clause [3].

The memo also notes that clause 7.3 of the Services Agreement records the parties' agreement that the amounts are "a reasonable pre-estimate of those losses and not a penalty" [3].

turns.question: What delivery date did the Services Agreement originally set?
turns.text:
The Services Agreement (DEMO) originally set the Delivery Date as May 15, 2026. This is stated in clause 4.2 of the Services Agreement, which says: "4.2 Delivery Date. The Supplier shall deliver all Units to the Delivery Point on or before May 15, 2026." [2]

Later, Amendment No. 1 changed the Delivery Date to May 20, 2026. This is confirmed in clause 1.1 of Amendment No. 1, which states: "1.1 Clause 4.2 of the Services Agreement is deleted and replaced with: '4.2 Delivery Date. The Supplier shall deliver all Units to the Delivery Point on or before May 20, 2026.'" [6]
notes: Clause 4.2 of Services Agreement (DEMO) was deleted and replaced by clause 1.1 of Amendment No. 1 (DEMO) (signed). It says: “This Amendment takes effect on May 14, 2026, the date on which it has been signed by both Parties.”

Clause 7.1 of Services Agreement (DEMO) was deleted and replaced by clause 2.1 of Amendment No. 1 (DEMO) (signed). It says: “This Amendment takes effect on May 14, 2026, the date on which it has been signed by both Parties.”

turns.question: Is that still the date?
turns.text:
The Delivery Date was amended to May 20, 2026. This is confirmed by Amendment No. 1, which states, "The Delivery Date for all purposes of the Agreement, including clauses 7 and 11.3 of the Agreement, is May 20, 2026" [3]. Additionally, the same amendment mentions that the Delivery Date was changed from the original date of May 15, 2026 [5].

The documents also indicate that the Delivery Date was not changed after the amendment. The amendment took effect on May 14, 2026, and the Delivery Date remained May 20, 2026 [4].
cited: Notice of late delivery and claim (DEMO)

turns.question: What else did that amendment change?
turns.text: Amendment No. 1 changed two specific clauses in the Services Agreement. It replaced clause 4.2 to set the Delivery Date as May 20, 2026 [2]. It also changed clause 7.1 to set the liquidated damages at 1.5% per week [3].

turns.question: When did Apex dispatch the units?
turns.text:
Apex dispatched the units on May 10, 2026, as stated in an email from Priya Raman, Program Manager at Apex, which provided the planned dispatch date of May 10, 2026 [6].

The email also stated that the estimated arrival was on the morning of May 15, 2026 [6].

Additionally, Mr. Pell recalled that the units arrived at Dock 3 on May 12, 2026 [2]. However, Apex claims that all forty units arrived on May 15, 2026 [4].

The Delivery Date was amended to May 20, 2026, according to Amendment No. 1 [10].
notes: Clause 4.2 of Services Agreement (DEMO) was deleted and replaced by clause 1.1 of Amendment No. 1 (DEMO) (signed). It says: “This Amendment takes effect on May 14, 2026, the date on which it has been signed by both Parties.”

turns.question: And when did they arrive?
turns.text: The units were delivered in two stages. The initial delivery of all forty Units occurred on May 15, 2026, as stated in the notice of late delivery and claim [4]. However, Delivery was not complete until the replacement Units arrived on June 10, 2026. This is because two Units were rejected on May 18, 2026, and their replacements were delivered on June 10, 2026 [4].
